clue.text: A tramp going about left series of tracks

indicators.note: A and the tramp together go round, enclosing the next piece

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A vagrant wanders off, leaving a trail of footprints behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a collection of recorded songs, so a series of tracks on one release.

clue.text: Language used by joiners in plant

indicators.note: the language belongs to the joiners, so their word comes first in a possessive

parts.note: adders join numbers together when they add them up
a tongue is a language

explanation.surface: Carpenters have their own jargon for talking about timber and vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiners' suggests carpenters, but adders join numbers together by adding.
explanation.definitionFit: Adder's-tongue is a small fern, a species of plant found in damp grassland.

clue.text: Employ sound censorship method

definitions.meaning: to make a short high electronic noise, as a pager does
a tone dubbed over swear words on broadcast television

explanation.surface: A broadcaster adopts a solid approach to cutting rude words.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both emitting an electronic tone and masking an expletive with such a tone on air.

clue.text: Sauce stain that's appeared

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blemish, like a stain
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
rose means came up or appeared

explanation.surface: A cook notices a sauce mark that has suddenly shown up on the tablecloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Rose is the pink seafood dressing served with a prawn cocktail.

clue.text: Steps for which I apologise

definitions.meaning: a ballroom dance in which a partner may be cut in on, so a set of dance steps
the polite phrase said when begging pardon

explanation.surface: Someone says sorry for treading on another's feet while dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a dance where one cuts in on couples and a polite apology.

clue.text: Empty eggshells of two or more colours, and spotted

indicators.note: emptying the word removes its inside, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: pied means patchy in two or more colours, like a magpie

explanation.surface: Someone describes hollow, mottled eggshells found in a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Espied is a past tense meaning caught sight of, exactly as spotted means seen.

clue.text: Stop that peddler pinching pretty girl's NONE bottom!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Stop that peddler pinching pretty girl's NONE bottom!': 'NONE' is OCR garbage and the scan is blank; CUTI(E) + TOUT needs a word removing the girl's last letter that the clue as held does not give
annotationWithheld.clue: Stop that peddler pinching pretty girl's NONE bottom!

clue.text: Weapon peacemaker could turn to shareholders' advantage?

definitions.text: Weapon peacemaker could turn to shareholders' advantage?

parts.words: Weapon peacemaker could turn to shareholders' advantage?
parts.note: alludes to the biblical beating of blades into ploughshares; shareholders hints at those ploughshares

explanation.surface: An arms dealer turned pacifist finds a way to make money for investors.
explanation.definitionFit: The bladed weapon is the one Isaiah says will be beaten into ploughshares in peacetime.

clue.text: Blue but no less absorbing musical

indicators.note: no means take away the letters that follow from the show's title
the word less wraps around the rest of the title, its letters forming the outside

parts.note: Les Misérables is the long-running musical based on Hugo's novel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A downbeat review of a show that holds the audience no less.
explanation.walkthrough: LES MISERABLES has L-E-S at the front and S at the end: that outer LESS 'absorbs' the middle, so removing it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means unhappy or wretched, a synonym of the adjective given.

clue.text: Prove perks don't work for Ukrainian city

indicators.note: the letters are worked or made to operate in a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving its four letters

explanation.surface: An unhappy employee argues that fringe benefits fail in a factory town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't work' looks like a phrase, but 'don't' is fodder and 'work' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dnipropetrovsk was the Soviet-era name of Dnipro, a large industrial city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Get hard stone fragments as tank obstacles

indicators.note: breaking into fragments rearranges the preceding words' letters

explanation.surface: Engineers smash tough rock to build barriers against armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of concrete pyramids built to stop tanks in wartime were named after the teeth of a mythical beast.

clue.text: Theatre with grudge put on show

indicators.note: with joins the two parts side by side in clue order

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
to resent is to bear a grudge

explanation.surface: A bitter actor stages his performance at the local playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent is to depict or exhibit, so to place something on display.

clue.text: Painter of the French posterior no ace

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

indicators.note: no means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: the rear is the posterior or backside
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A gallery note mentions a French artist's portrait of a backside without its best feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the great German Renaissance artist and engraver.

clue.text: Closed luggage compartment, furthermore

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
in British usage the boot is a car's trunk

explanation.surface: Someone notes the car trunk has been shut, as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOT is the British word for a car's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in addition or moreover, as an extra point is added.

clue.text: Fundamentalist tract's bitterness about bishop going on strike

definitions.note: possessive 's here reads as 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in a down entry the later piece goes on underneath the first
the word for bitterness goes around the bishop's letter

parts.note: bile is bitterness or bad temper
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to belt is to hit or strike

explanation.surface: A church pamphlet rails angrily against a cleric who has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tract' looks like a pamphlet but means a region of land.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of the southern USA where evangelical Protestantism dominates is a tract of land known for fundamentalism.

clue.text: Hanger for placing hooks on?

parts.note: reads like a peg for coats, but hooks are boxing punches and the hanger is a suspended training sack

explanation.surface: A rail or peg on which hooks might be hung.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer practises hooks and other blows on a heavy suspended sack in the gym.

clue.text: Tory swore in confusion after poll blow?

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory
cussed is an informal word for swore

explanation.surface: A Conservative curses in bewilderment after a setback at the election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' looks like an election but is an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dazed after a knock on the head is the state of mild brain injury described.

clue.text: Plants hint of cherry in mixed raisins

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the reshuffled word
mixed means the letters of the dried fruit are jumbled
a hint of a word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A baker stirs a little cherry into a bowl of dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles RAISINS; 'in' places C, from 'hint of cherry', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: These are daffodils and related spring bulbs, plural of the genus name.

clue.text: He symbolises one with imposing air

parts.note: noble means grand or imposing
air is a gas

explanation.surface: A man stands for someone with a grand and lofty manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun but is the chemical symbol for helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium, symbol He, is one of the inert elements in group 18 of the periodic table.

clue.text: Foreign language text removed from the Observer

definitions.meaning: a passage given to students for translation at sight, without preparation
not seen by the one watching, out of sight

explanation.surface: A translation passage has been cut from a Sunday newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, which makes the second sense look like a press story.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an exam passage translated at sight and an adjective for not witnessed.

clue.text: Rolls off the production line here

definitions.text: Rolls off the production line here

parts.words: Rolls off the production line here
parts.note: suggests a car factory, but the rolls are bread made where loaves are baked

explanation.surface: A car factory where luxury Rolls-Royces leave the assembly line.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where bread rolls are produced is a baker's premises.

clue.text: Topple like a jockey before the finish

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a jockey riding in a race is said to be up
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A horse rider is thrown off just short of the winning post.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it over or knock it down.

clue.text: Coffee winningly served up strong

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tennis player who aced served an unreturnable ball
F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong

explanation.surface: A tennis champion is brought a cup of robust coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is the short name for coffee with its caffeine removed.

clue.text: Smashed up central Bucks

indicators.note: bucks as a verb, the letters kick about like a bucking horse

explanation.surface: Somebody's gone wild in the middle of Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' looks like Buckinghamshire, an English county, but it is the verb, signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulent describes someone ill from heavy drinking, matching smashed meaning very drunk.

clue.text: Be chauvinistic, ignoring first son

indicators.note: ignoring first means the opening letter, given by son, is dropped

parts.note: a male chauvinist is sexist
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A father tells his eldest to stop being a male chauvinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Exist is a synonym of be in its sense of having reality or life.

clue.text: Cricket team to take on after woolly jumpers in the field

indicators.note: after means the hiring part follows the sheep

parts.note: Leicesters are a breed of long-wooled sheep, which jump in fields
to hire is to take on staff

explanation.surface: A county side recruits players after spotting sweaters in the outfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly jumpers' suggests sweaters, and 'field' cricket, but these are sheep in a pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicestershire County Cricket Club plays in England's first-class county championship.

clue.text: Topless girl put on things in heavy fashion

indicators.note: the girl's piece is put on after the first piece

parts.note: stuff means things or belongings

indicators.note: with its top removed, the name loses its first letter

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman without a top is dressed up in heavy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffily means in a stodgy, airless or pompous manner, so heavily.

clue.text: Like some cheese, mate?

definitions.meaning: from the Netherlands, as Edam and Gouda are
in Cockney slang, 'my old ...' is a wife or partner

explanation.surface: A friend asks whether some cheese is of a particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Dutch, from 'duchess', is Cockney rhyming slang for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers produce from Holland and the London slang word for a man's spouse.
